intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO daily as a PIK3CA-directed adjunct, sequenced into the post-HIPEC window and held peri-operatively
expected_benefit: ALASCCA time-to-recurrence HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24-0.98) in the PIK3CA exon-9/20 subset (Group A), 3-yr recurrence 7.7% vs 14.1%; direction replicated by celecoxib in the PIK3CA-activated subset of CALGB/SWOG 80702 (DFS HR 0.56, OS HR 0.41) and Liao observational (CRC-specific mortality HR 0.18).
key_risks: G3+ GI bleeding ~3% (vs ~2% placebo) in ALASCCA
bleeding-timing interaction with concurrent bevacizumab and the planned CRS-HIPEC operative window
preference_alignment: oral, matches surface-everything intake and empty toxicity_vetoes; efficacy weight 0.70 favors a real biomarker-matched signal; prefers_trials PARTIAL (this is an off-label adjunct, not a trial referral)
guideline_status: NCCN adopted ALASCCA for resected stage II-III PIK3CA-mutant disease as adjuvant therapy; off-label by indication for stage IV metastatic disease
rationale_summary: The one RoB-low randomized phase-3 on the board where the biomarker matches the patient: ALASCCA (pmid:40961426, n=626) put M1043I into its exon-9/20 Group A and hit HR 0.49, with concordant direction from celecoxib in 80702 (pmid:38889377) and the Liao cohort (pmid:23094721). The critic and concensusite ranked it first for exactly this reason, and the conservative endorsed it as the do-no-harm biomarker-matched adjunct. The load-bearing limit every persona named is the indication gap: ALASCCA randomized resected stage I-III, not active stage IV peritoneal disease, so the biology travels but the effect size does not, which is why this is a post-HIPEC adjuvant-equivalent adjunct rather than antitumor therapy for the metastatic compartment. The risktaker dissented on rank, not on use, arguing an efficacy-weighted patient with a real KRAS driver should not have an adjuvant-setting adjunct at the top slot; the objection is about ordering, and the adjunct still layers cheaply onto whatever backbone runs. Hold peri-operatively per surgical protocol and re-time into the post-HIPEC maintenance window where the ALASCCA evidence actually lives.
open_questions: Whether M1043I is somatic and clonal on the pending NGS (a subclonal PIK3CA call weakens the Group A read-across)
Whether the resected-adjuvant effect size transfers at all to active peritoneal metastatic disease
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate as a recurrence-risk adjunct: ALASCCA HR 0.49 in the exon-9/20 subset M1043I maps into; direction concordant across three datasets, but validated in resected not metastatic disease.

counter_productive_moa.description: Additive bleeding risk with concurrent bevacizumab and the CRS-HIPEC window; a sequencing/timing hold, not a mechanism that blunts the therapeutic goal.

overall: The strongest RoB-low biomarker match and a do-no-harm PIK3CA-directed adjunct; effect validated in resected, not metastatic, disease, so it layers on the backbone rather than replacing it.

intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab (Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 + anti-PD-1), 2L+ after FOLFIRI-bev progression, on an MSS-CRC / any-KRAS protocol (USC NCT06336902, Agenus NCT05608044, CCTG NCT07152821, or expanded access NCT06751524)
expected_benefit: Bullock 2024 (n=101): all-comer MSS mCRC ORR 17% (95% CI 10-26); no-liver-metastasis subset ORR 22% with mOS 20.9 mo vs 5% ORR in the active-liver-mets subset. The randomized phase-2 update (n=123 NLM) held the combination at ORR 19% and specifically reported confirmed responses at peritoneal sites.
key_risks: overall G3+ irAE ~35-38% with characteristic pyrexia/cytokine-release; no treatment-related deaths reported (0/101)
preference_alignment: prefers_trials YES (named on-axis MSS/any-KRAS protocols surfaced); efficacy weight 0.70 favors chasing a 20%+ compartment-matched response; empty toxicity_vetoes means the ~35% irAE rate is a counseling burden, not a hard filter; IV modality with no modality_constraints
guideline_status: Investigational; no NCCN category for bot/bal in MSS mCRC yet - CCTG NCT07152821 vs BSC is the confirmatory phase 3
rationale_summary: The one immunotherapy option with a real MSS-CRC signal at this patient's exact disease compartment: peritoneal-dominant disease after liver-met resection is the no-liver-mets phenotype where Bullock 2024 (pmid:38871975) hit ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo, and the randomized update called out confirmed peritoneal-site responses. MSS/TMB-low/PD-L1-negative normally closes single-agent ICI, but Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 is the one construct with a genuine MSS signal, so the risktaker, conservative, critic and advocate all ranked it and none dissented. Two constraints keep it at considered_with_caveats rather than a clean recommendation: the toxicity envelope (~35-38% G3+ irAE, colitis and hepatitis) in a patient also heading into major cytoreductive surgery, and the sequencing gate - every biomarker-eligible protocol requires prior fluoropyrimidine/oxaliplatin/irinotecan progression, so this activates 2L+ after FOLFIRI-bev, not now. The peritoneal-site and NLM numbers are subgroup figures without CIs from a single-arm phase 1b plus a phase 2 whose comparator is monotherapy, which the critic held to grade; the CCTG phase 3 is the pending confirmatory test. Enroll only at a center with a standing steroid/infliximab irAE algorithm.
open_questions: Whether the peritoneal cavity's milky-spot immunobiology tracks the liver-met-derived response data
Whether the NLM/peritoneal subgroup signal survives the randomized CCTG phase-3 readout against BSC
The USC protocol requires prior oxaliplatin, which the FOLFIRI-bev history does not yet include - realistic entry is post-1L-progression or post-HIPEC
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate in this NLM/peritoneal subset: ORR ~22% and mOS 20.9 mo (Bullock 2024), the strongest MSS-CRC ICI signal, but subgroup-level and not yet confirmed vs BSC.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (immune-mediated colitis 12-13%, hepatitis ~8%, pyrexia/cytokine-release; overall G3+ irAE ~35-38%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 irAE colitis/hepatitis overlaps the peri-operative CRS window; immune-mediated toxicity could delay or complicate cytoreductive surgery.

overall: The only MSS-CRC immunotherapy with a compartment-matched signal at the patient's peritoneal disease; a 2L+ proposition gated by ~35% immune toxicity and single-arm, subgroup-level evidence.

intervention_label: Mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibition - CGT6297 on the explicit CRC + PIK3CA cohort (NCT07383506, Cohort 3), with tersolisib (NCT05768139) / ETX-636 (NCT06993844) / inavolisib+bev on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223) as class alternatives
expected_benefit: No RCT-grade CRC efficacy for any PI3K-alpha agent. Cross-tumor anchor INAVO120 (breast) PFS HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.32-0.59); mutant-selective abstracts report kinase-domain-PIK3CA activity (RLY-2608 ORR 66.7%, 95% CI 38.4-88.2; tersolisib 21% all-comer, both breast/gyn); the closest CRC readout is 2 PRs in the CRC subset of alpelisib's n=134 (~6% ORR, pmid:29401002).
key_risks: Class hyperglycemia - G3+ ~20% on alpelisib (pmid:29401002), ~6% on inavolisib, and near-zero on the wild-type-sparing mutant-selective agents in abstract data
stomatitis, rash, diarrhea (attenuated in the mutant-selective generation)
hyperglycemia management overlaps poorly with the peri-operative window
preference_alignment: prefers_trials YES (CGT6297 is the one trial that names a CRC-and-PIK3CA cohort by protocol text, not a breast read-across); oral; efficacy weight 0.70 tempered by thin CRC efficacy; empty toxicity_vetoes
guideline_status: Investigational / off-label; no approved PI3K-alpha indication in CRC (inavolisib approved in HR+/HER2- breast only)
rationale_summary: The cleanest PIK3CA-and-CRC match on the board: CGT6297's phase-1b Cohort 3 names PIK3CA-mutant colorectal cancer explicitly, and M1043I is a kinase-domain activating allele that fits the oncogenic-mutation gate, which is why the advocate and risktaker ranked the mutant-selective class high and the conservative and critic carried it as a low-confidence 2L-reserve. The wall is evidence: every efficacy readout for this axis is cross-tumor - INAVO120 (pmid:39476340) is breast, RLY-2608 and tersolisib are breast/gyn conference abstracts, and the only CRC data is 2 alpelisib PRs (pmid:29401002). Predictive confidence for a rarer non-canonical kinase-domain allele like M1043I is lower than for canonical H1047R, and KRAS A59T co-activation historically blunts single-agent PI3K-alpha response in CRC, so the honest expectation is best-case activity in combination or in the wild-type-sparing generation, not proven monotherapy benefit. No persona vetoed or formally dissented, but the uniform cross-tumor / abstract-tier caveat and the M1043I predictive-confidence hedge hold this at considered_with_caveats. The mutant-selective agents (tersolisib, ETX-636) trade the alpelisib metabolic burden for a cleaner but still abstract-only safety profile.
open_questions: Whether CRC Cohort 3 of NCT07383506 is open and accruing
Whether response at the non-canonical M1043I allele tracks the canonical H1047R/E545K data the class was built on
Whether vertical KRAS + PI3K-alpha co-blockade is needed given A59T co-activation, and at what added toxicity
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate for CRC: cross-tumor kinase-domain-PIK3CA signal (INAVO120 HR 0.43 in breast; RLY-2608 ORR 66.7% breast) with only 2 alpelisib CRC PRs and a non-canonical-allele hedge.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (hyperglycemia G3+ ~20% alpelisib / ~6% inavolisib, stomatitis, rash, diarrhea; near-absent on wild-type-sparing agents)

counter_productive_moa.description: KRAS A59T co-activation can bypass PI3K-alpha blockade via parallel MAPK signaling, blunting single-agent response and arguing for combination.

overall: The one trial naming a CRC-and-PIK3CA cohort, targeting the patient's kinase-domain allele directly; efficacy rests entirely on cross-tumor abstract-tier data with a non-canonical-allele predictive hedge.

intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) and other codon-agnostic pan-RAS / RAS(ON) inhibitors on trials whose eligibility does not name a codon (Pfizer PF-07934040 NCT06447662 'any KRAS variant', Roche RO7673396 NCT06884618, Jacobio JAB-23E73 NCT06973564, Adlai AN9025 NCT07252479, RevMed RAS(ON)+ivonescimab NCT07397338), contingent on a sponsor A59T-eligibility call
expected_benefit: No A59T-specific efficacy data exists. Peer-reviewed pivotal data is PDAC on canonical codons: daraxonrasib 2L RAS-G12 ORR 35% (95% CI 17-56, n=26), G12/G13/Q61 ORR 29% (pmid:42090791). The RAS-mutant CRC monotherapy signal is a company-disclosed ORR ~9% (30-Sep-2024 cutoff, no N, no CI, null identifier). A59T applicability is a structural read-across from Knox 2025 (pmid:40056080), which tested WT + G12/G13/Q61 but not A59T.
key_risks: Daraxonrasib monotherapy G3+ treatment-related AEs ~30% in PDAC (rash, stomatitis/mucositis, diarrhea; pmid:42090791)

the ivonescimab (PD-1/VEGF) and cetuximab combination arms stack overlapping GI/rash/hepatic toxicity with no CRC combination-toxicity dataset, and the VEGF-axis agent argues for holding until the CRS-HIPEC wound-healing window has passed
preference_alignment: prefers_trials YES and this is the only class that reaches the patient's actual KRAS A59T driver; efficacy weight 0.70 and empty toxicity_vetoes favor the swing; but the eligibility win is codon-agnostic protocol text pending sponsor confirmation, not demonstrated A59T activity
guideline_status: Off-guideline for the specific asset; NCCN routes A59T mCRC to trial enrollment (category 2A) as a pathway, but attaches no category to daraxonrasib or any A59T regimen
rationale_summary: The only asset class that mechanistically reaches KRAS A59T: RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitors bind GTP-loaded RAS at a CypA-SWI/SWII pocket outside the mutated codon groove (pmid:40056080), so a switch-II A59T is a plausible extension, and the newly-surfaced codon-agnostic baskets (PF-07934040 reads 'any KRAS variant') finally give the allele a trial door. The risktaker and advocate ranked it first on that basis, with the sponsor A59T-eligibility call flagged as the highest-leverage single action. Three personas dissented and the reason is uniform: A59T applicability is a structural read-across, not efficacy data. The peer-reviewed pivotal readout (pmid:42090791) is PDAC on codons 12/13/61, the CRC monotherapy number is a ~9% company-disclosed ORR without N or CI, and no trial has ever dosed an A59T patient - the conservative and critic dissented on evidence quality and the conservative additionally on the uncharacterized combination toxicity, while the concensusite dissented on guideline-fit (an investigational agent ranked as if standard). The distinction load-bearing here: codon-agnostic eligibility is an enrollment question that turns on a sponsor phone call, not proof the drug works on this allele; pan-RAS assets must not be presented as proven in A59T. It stays in the ranking because dropping a veto-free, feature-targeting trial referral the patient prefers would hide what the board genuinely considered - but at considered_with_caveats, framed as a mechanism bet and a trial referral, sequenced after 1L progression and outside the VEGF-axis wound-healing window. The RAS(ON)+ivonescimab suite (NCT07397338) mixes codon-selective elironrasib/zoldonrasib that are mechanism-mismatched to A59T, so lead with the codon-agnostic daraxonrasib/PF-07934040 gates.
open_questions: Whether any sponsor accepts a switch-II A59 allele as a qualifying RAS mutation (the make-or-break enrollment question)
Whether pan-RAS binders optimized against G12/G13 actually engage the switch-II A59T site with meaningful pathway suppression
Combination toxicity of daraxonrasib + ivonescimab plus/minus cetuximab in CRC, for which no dataset exists
likelihood_of_effect: Low / unquantified for A59T: zero allele-matched data; extrapolated from PDAC canonical-codon ORR 35% (pmid:42090791) and structural binding (pmid:40056080, A59T untested); CRC monotherapy signal ~9%.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (daraxonrasib G3+ TRAE ~30%: rash, stomatitis/mucositis, diarrhea; combination arms uncharacterized in CRC)

counter_productive_moa.description: Switch-II A59T may signal weakly through MAPK, so pan-RAS engagement optimized for G12/G13 could under-suppress the pathway; VEGF-arm wound-healing impairment peri-HIPEC.

overall: The only option reaching the patient's actual KRAS A59T driver, but on codon-agnostic eligibility and structural read-across with zero allele-matched efficacy; a sponsor-gated trial referral, not proven A59T therapy.
